$comment: Language servers of this pack. `config` is the fragment `factory init` merges into the app repo's .factory/config.json (lsp.servers entries, see docs/code-intelligence.md for every field). `optional` holds further fragments to merge by hand. `install` says how to get each server's binary, per OS (`all` = every OS); `factory lsp setup` prints these lines for a server it cannot find. `verified` says whether this file was proven by running the server through the factory or written from the server's documentation.

verified.how: Not run: this machine has rustup but no installed toolchain. Written from the rust-analyzer manual. The engine path it uses (a leased server without reportsState, started under scripts/lsp/launch.mjs) is covered by the engine tests with a fake server.

leased.rust: yes: rust-analyzer keeps the whole cargo workspace and its dependencies in memory and runs cargo check; several of them at once exhaust a machine.

all: rustup component add rust-analyzer rust-src   # follows the toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, so the server matches the compiler
macos: brew install rust-analyzer   # alternative without rustup
linux: curl -L https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/releases/latest/download/rust-analyzer-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.gz | gunzip -c > ~/.local/bin/rust-analyzer && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/rust-analyzer   # alternative without rustup

requires: cargo and the pinned toolchain; add ~/.cargo/bin to project.toolPaths (hooks and background runs do not load the shell profile)
notes: Optional prepare so the first request does not wait for downloads: "prepare": {"command": "cargo", "args": ["fetch", "--locked"], "label": "fetching crates"}.
No scope module: rust-analyzer loads the workspace it finds from the opened file. A linked git worktree has its own target/ directory, so the first cargo check there is a full build.
Without reportsState the daemon cannot tell loading from ready: requests made while the workspace loads wait up to lsp.callTimeoutSec and then answer "rust language server unavailable".
